q: The base of a right prism is an isosceles trapezium with parallel sides measuring 10 cm and 20 cm, and non-parallel sides measuring 13 cm each. The volume of the prism is 3240 cm³ . What is the total surface area of the prism?
solution:
Shortcut Trick

Height of trapezium = √(13² − 5²) = 12 cm

Base area = 1/2 × (10 + 20) × 12 = 180 cm²

TSA = 2 × Base area + Perimeter × Prism height

∴ The correct answer is 1368 cm².

Calculations:

⇒ The base of the right-angled triangle formed by dropping a perpendicular = (20 − 10) ÷ 2 = 5 cm

⇒ By Pythagoras theorem, height of trapezium, hₜ = √(13² − 5²) = √(169 − 25) = √144 = 12 cm

⇒ Area of trapezium base = 1/2 × (10 + 20) × 12 = 1/2 × 30 × 12 = 180 cm²

⇒ Total Surface Area = 2 × Area of base + Lateral Surface Area

⇒ Total Surface Area = 2 × 180 + 1008 = 360 + 1008 = 1368 cm²

∴ The correct answer is 1368 cm².
